question: A 26-year-old nurse presents 12 hours after she accidentally stuck herself with a blood-contaminated needle. She reported the accident appropriately and now seeks post-exposure prophylaxis. She does not have any complaints at the moment of presentation. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 125/80 mm Hg, heart rate 71/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and temperature 36.5℃ (97.7℉). Physical examination is unremarkable. The nurse has prescribed a post-exposure prophylaxis regimen which includes tenofovir, emtricitabine, and raltegravir. How will tenofovir change the maximum reaction rate (Vm) and Michaelis constant (Km) of the viral reverse transcriptase?

options.opa: Vm will decrease, Km will stay the same
options.opb: Vm and Km will both decrease
options.opc: Vm will decrease, Km will increase
options.opd: Vm will stay the same, Km will increase
options.ope: Vm and Km will both increase

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Tenofovir is a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor" -> "inhibits viral reverse transcriptase activity" -> "reduces the maximum reaction rate (Vm)" -> "Km remains unchanged due to competitive inhibition" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Tenofovir binds to reverse transcriptase" -> "prevents viral RNA from being converted to DNA" -> "decreases the maximum reaction rate (Vm)" -> "Km does not change as it is not a substrate" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Tenofovir acts on viral reverse transcriptase" -> "inhibits enzyme function" -> "leads to a decrease in Vm" -> "Km remains constant as it does not affect substrate affinity" -> 88%
CHAIN: "Tenofovir is a competitive inhibitor of reverse transcriptase" -> "competes with natural substrates" -> "reduces Vm" -> "Km remains the same as it does not alter binding affinity" -> 87%
analysis: Tenofovir is a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that competes with the natural substrate for the active site of the viral reverse transcriptase enzyme. When an inhibitor like tenofovir is present, it can decrease the maximum reaction rate (Vm) because the enzyme's activity is reduced due to the competition for the substrate. The Michaelis constant (Km) may increase because the presence of the inhibitor can lead to a higher concentration of substrate being required to reach half of the maximum reaction rate. Therefore, Vm will decrease and Km will increase.
